- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust upward if recent history shows persistent downward drift.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 60+ → 70+), then fail to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak or use moving average smoothing.
- Lagged response to true price movements: model reacts 1–2 days too slowly; add 1–2 day lag correction or use 3-day rolling average for smoothing.
- High variance in short-term forecasts (e.g., 30d) — reduce volatility by applying exponential smoothing or median filter to avoid overfitting to noise.
- When true price rises >10% from 30d mean, reduce forecast slope to avoid runaway growth; apply diminishing returns multiplier (e.g., 0.8x for >70% increase).
